tool_input.command: for s in rotate.sh verify.sh; do bash "$s" --help >/dev/null 2>&1; echo "$s --help rc=$?"; bash "$s" --dest 2>&1 >/dev/null | tail -1; bash "$s" --dest /no/such/dir --name x -q 2>&1 >/dev/null | tail -1; bash "$s" --dest /tmp --name x --bogus 2>&1 >/dev/null | tail -1; done
tool_input.description: Smoke-test flags and exit codes of rotate.sh and verify.sh

result:
Everything checks out: all 12 tests pass, both refactored scripts keep accepting the same flags (`--dest`, `--dest=`, `--name`, `--keep`, `-q/--quiet`, `-n/--dry-run`, `-h/--help`, `--`, unknown-option → exit 1, missing dir → exit 2), and log lines are still prefixed with the script name. `backup.sh`, `restore.sh`, `report.sh` were left untouched.

What was done:
- **rotate.sh** — `surplus()` used `tail -n +"$keep"` on an oldest-first list, deleting the newest archives; it now deletes the oldest `total - keep` entries (`head -n`), and `total == keep` short-circuits to "nothing to rotate".
- **verify.sh** — the sidecar file name was extracted with `awk '{print $2}'`, truncating at spaces; it now uses `read -r expected file` (first word, then the rest of the line), and the digest comparison is quoted.
- **lib/common.sh** — new file holding the shared option-parsing block (as `parse_common_args`) and `resolve_dir`, sourced by rotate.sh and verify.sh.
- **tests/run_tests.sh** — regression tests for both bugs (intact archive with a space in its name → ok/rc=0; `--keep 3` with exactly 3 archives deletes nothing, `--keep 2` drops the oldest and its sidecar).

Changed: `rotate.sh`, `verify.sh`, `tests/run_tests.sh`, and new `lib/common.sh`.
